title: National MILO Marathon 2026 Cebu Leg Review: What the 2026 Race Was Like
seo_title: MILO Marathon Cebu Leg 2026 Review: Haze, Heat, Cut-offs, Pace
meta_description: MILO Marathon Cebu leg 2026 review: the Mandaue 21 km and 10 km, 28°C and a 24°C dew point before dawn, haze rated unhealthy for sensitive groups, the 2:30 cut-off and how fast the field ran.
dek: What it was like to run the 50th MILO Marathon's Cebu leg in Mandaue on 6 September 2026: the course, the pre-dawn heat and the haze, the cut-offs, how fast the field ran, and the route to the National Finals.
verdict: Enter if you are near Cebu and want a cheap, timed 21 km or 10 km with a route to the National MILO Marathon Finals. The 2026 Mandaue leg drew 10,000 registered runners, but only 170 are listed in the 21 km results, where 1:32 was enough for tenth among men and 2:20 for tenth among women. The catch is the air and the clock. Before dawn it was 27°C to 28°C with a 24°C dew point, haze kept air quality in the unhealthy-for-sensitive-groups band, and the 21 km closes at two and a half hours, with a 90-minute check at 10 km. Enter the 21 km only if you can finish inside 2:30, and watch the haze readings in race week.

sections.heading: The Course: Round Mandaue from Gatewalk Central
paragraphs: The 2026 Cebu leg started and finished at Gatewalk Central in Mandaue City, with the route running around the streets of Mandaue before returning to the start [1][2]. The distances were 21 km, 10 km, 5 km and 3 km [1], plus a 5 km family category and 3 km, 5 km and 10 km races for runners with disabilities [3].

No route map, elevation profile or aid-station plan was on the race pages. The 2026 rules say the route map can be viewed on the official MILO website and that gun times for each category would be announced later [4]; the MILO marathon page carried neither [5]. The Race Roster listing gives the event as starting at 3am [3].
Only the 21 km and 10 km are chip-timed; the chip is attached to the back of the bib [3].

sections.heading: The Weather and the Haze
paragraphs: Mactan-Cebu International Airport, roughly 6 km east of the start across the Mactan Channel, recorded 28°C at 3am on race morning, with a dew point of 24°C, 79% humidity and a 9-knot wind [6]. It dipped to 27°C at 5am and 6am, when humidity peaked at 89% with a dew point of 25°C, then warmed quickly: 30°C at 7am and 31°C at 8am [6].

A dew point of 24°C to 25°C is air so wet that sweat barely evaporates, so even a pre-dawn 21 km is a hot race. Anyone still running after 6am ran into rising heat: the temperature climbed three degrees in the hour to 7am [6].

In 2026 the air mattered as much as the heat. Smoke from forest fires in Kalimantan pushed Metro Cebu's PM2.5 air quality index to 252 on 3 September, the highest of the episode and worse than the October 2015 haze [7]. The race went ahead despite pre-race concerns about the haze [2]. By race morning it had eased: the Environmental Management Bureau (EMB 7) recorded 126 at 7am on Sunday, in the 'Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups' band, in which children, older adults and people with heart or respiratory conditions are advised to limit prolonged or strenuous outdoor activity [8].

EMB 7's monitoring that month found fine particles rising from midnight until about 8am and falling from 10am [9], which covers the whole of a race listed from 3am [3]. The leg is held in early September; if haze is being reported in race week, check EMB 7's readings. In 2026 residents were told to wear properly fitted N95 or KN95 masks outdoors [9].

sections.heading: Cut-offs and Rules: Two and a Half Hours for the 21 km
paragraphs: The 21 km closes 2 hours 30 minutes after the last runner crosses the start line, the 10 km after two hours, and the 5 km and 3 km after one hour [4][3]. The 21 km also has a check: runners who have not reached 10 km within 90 minutes must stop, board the official vehicle and are disqualified [4].

Medals go only to 21 km and 10 km finishers inside the cut-off [3]. The rules say every 21 km finisher gets the loot bag and finisher's shirt, but only those inside the limit get the medal and certificate [4]. In 2026 the results list 24 timed 21 km runners slower than 2:30 [10].

Other rules are strict too. Bibs cannot be transferred, and a runner who lets someone else use their bib can be banned for a year; running with an unregistered pacer gets you disqualified; so does not starting within 10 minutes of your flag-off [4]. Winners are decided on gun time [4]. The 21 km is for runners 18 and over, with a fit-to-run medical certificate signed by a doctor within two months of race day; the 10 km is for 16 and over [4].

sections.heading: How Fast the Field Is
paragraphs: Jhonn Marc Dizon won the 21 km in 1:13:26 gun time, ahead of Janry Pelones in 1:15:17 and Jerome Casinillo in 1:16:40 [10]. Michelle Zamora won the women's race in 1:32:40, from the Olympian and former multi-time MILO champion Mary Joy Tabal in 1:44:45 and Mericel Cabrera in 1:48:06 [10][2]. The press gave Dizon's time as one hour 12 minutes and Zamora's as 1:32:00 [11][12]; the times here are the published gun times. The Freeman reported that Dizon was defending the 21 km title, and that both winners are University of San Carlos athletes [11].

Behind the front three the field thins fast. The fourth man ran 1:26:58, the tenth 1:32:42, and the tenth woman 2:19:38 [10]. Only eight runners broke 1:30 and 64 broke two hours; the median 21 km time was 2:05:51 [10]. The 21 km results list 170 runners, only 29 of them women, and the 10 km 473 [10], so the results point to most of the 10,000 registered runners [2] taking part in the untimed 5 km and 3 km.

The 10 km was won in 34:57 by Mark Mahinay and in 43:16 by Ashley Faith Alburo, and 36 runners broke an hour [10]. Prize money in the 21 km is P10,000, P6,000 and P4,000 for the top three, and in the 10 km P5,000, P3,000 and P2,000 [4]. One rule matters for fast runners: anyone who finishes in the top ten of any race cannot run in the later MILO races that season [4].

sections.heading: The Road to the National Finals
paragraphs: The Cebu leg is a qualifier for the marathon at the National Finals in Clark City, Pampanga, on 6 December [3][11]. The male and female 21 km winners get an all-expenses place; everyone else qualifies by beating an age-group time, paying their own way but getting free entry, a free singlet and a ticket to the champions' dinner [4]. The standards start at 1:40 for men and 1:50 for women aged 18 to 34 and ease by about five minutes per age group [4].

In 2026 the results point to at least 33 runners inside their age-group standard [10]; SunStar's preview put the previous year's qualifiers at 40 [1]. Only Filipinos and foreigners with a working visa can win the 21 km qualifying races [4]. The top man and woman at the Finals earn a chance to represent the country at the Sydney Marathon the following year [1].

sections.heading: Race Weekend Logistics
paragraphs: Entry cost P1,799 for the 21 km, P1,599 for the 10 km, P699 for the 5 km and P499 for the 3 km, plus processing fees; the family 5 km cost P1,499 for three, P1,999 for four and P2,499 for five [3]. Entries are non-refundable, non-transferable and non-deferrable [3].

21 km runners get a singlet, bib, sports cap, finisher's medal, finisher's shirt, loot bag and e-certificate; 10 km runners the same without the shirt; 5 km and 3 km runners a singlet, bib and certificate [3]. The cap is collected on race day [3]. Race kits are claimed at an on-site event whose date and venue are announced a week before the race, and there is baggage deposit for the 10 km and 21 km only [4].
Full results for the 21 km and 10 km, with gun and chip times, were published on Race Roster [10]; the rules promise results within three working days [4].

sections.heading: Should You Enter the 2027 Cebu Leg?
paragraphs: Yes, if you are a Cebu runner who wants a cheap, timed 21 km or 10 km, a real chance at a top-ten place, or a qualifying time for the National Finals marathon. In 2026 a 1:32 man or a 2:20 woman made the 21 km top ten.

Think twice if you cannot run the 21 km inside 2:30, if you have asthma or a heart condition and haze is being reported, or if you want to know the route before you enter: no route map or start times were on the race pages in 2026.
The 2027 series calendar has not been published. The 2026 calendar noted that dates and venues are subject to change [3], so check where the Cebu leg is being held before you book.

Nobody from this site ran the race. This review draws on the organiser's race pages and rules, the full published results, airport weather records, air-quality reports, and local reporting in English and Cebuano.

faqs.question: Was the 2026 MILO Marathon Cebu leg run in haze?
faqs.answer: Yes, though it had eased. Smoke from Indonesian fires had pushed Metro Cebu's air quality index to 252 three days earlier. On race morning EMB 7 recorded 126 at 7am, 'Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups', a band in which children, older adults and people with heart or respiratory conditions are advised to limit strenuous outdoor activity.

faqs.question: How fast do you need to be to place at the MILO Marathon Cebu leg?
faqs.answer: Not very, outside the top three. In 2026 the 21 km was won in 1:13:26 and 1:32:40, but tenth place was 1:32:42 for men and 2:19:38 for women. Only 170 runners are listed in the 21 km results. Anyone finishing in the top ten cannot run the later MILO races that season.

faqs.question: What are the cut-off times at the MILO Marathon Cebu leg?
faqs.answer: Two and a half hours for the 21 km, two hours for the 10 km and one hour for the 5 km and 3 km. On the 21 km you must also reach 10 km within 90 minutes or board the official vehicle. Medals go only to 21 km and 10 km finishers inside the cut-off.

faqs.question: How do you qualify for the MILO Marathon National Finals from the Cebu leg?
faqs.answer: Win the 21 km, which earns an all-expenses place, or beat your age-group time, which earns free entry but not travel. The standards start at 1:40 for men and 1:50 for women aged 18 to 34. The 2026 National Finals marathon is in Clark City, Pampanga, on 6 December.

faqs.question: How hot is the MILO Marathon Cebu leg?
faqs.answer: Hot even before dawn. In 2026 Mactan airport recorded 28°C at 3am with a dew point of 24°C and 79% humidity, then 27°C and 89% humidity at 6am, 30°C at 7am and 31°C at 8am. Sweat barely evaporates in air that wet, so start slower than your usual race pace.

faqs.question: What do finishers get at the MILO Marathon Cebu leg?
faqs.answer: In 2026, 21 km runners got a singlet, bib, sports cap, loot bag and finisher's shirt, plus a medal and e-certificate if inside the cut-off. The 10 km got the same without the shirt; the 5 km and 3 km a singlet, bib and certificate. Entry was P1,799 for the 21 km.

editorial_notes: Rewritten 2026-09-29 about the 2026 Cebu leg, run on 6 September 2026 at Gatewalk Central, Mandaue City. Replaces a short results-only review. Weather is from airport METAR observations at Mactan-Cebu International Airport, not a forecast; the airport-to-start distance is a rough estimate from map coordinates. Air quality figures are EMB 7 readings as reported by SunStar. Field counts, the median, qualifying-standard counts and top-ten times are computed from the full Race Roster results; the 5 km and 3 km were not timed. Winning times are the published gun times; the press reported 1:12 and 1:32:00. Name spellings (Jhonn, Janry) follow the results and SunStar; The Freeman uses John and Jonry. No route map, start times or aid-station plan was published on the pages read, and no runner account of the 2026 race was found. The Manila Times report was not readable. No rating.
